articles.title: Post-its, homework breaks and karaoke: inside the Women’s Pro Baseball League’s debut season
articles.summary: The first league of its kind in 70 years brought players from all around the world to Illinois for eight weeks, writing a new chapter in the history of women’s sports.
body: On the morning of 14 September, Rocky Henley sat at her rental home’s dining room table amid scattered rulebooks, colorful markers and graph paper. The New York Heights manager drew a chart on a large poster – her method of sketching plays for the evening’s playoff game. Her assistant manager, Jackson, trudged in from the kitchen in flannel pajama pants and a Heights hoodie and watched her work. He also happens to be her son.

The Women’s Pro Baseball League (WPBL) is the first league of its kind in 70 years. Players hailed from across the US and 11 different countries to play for four teams: the Heights, Boston Hunters, San Francisco Firebells and Los Angeles Queens. While each team’s namesake city was selected for their market value and reputations for sports fandom, the eight-week inaugural season was played in entirety in Springfield, Illinois.
The inaugural season of the WPBL marked a pivotal moment in the women’s sports history books. The players, coaches and crew fashioned the paper, the pen and the ink to write this new chapter.

articles.title: All Blacks power past Australia to retain Bledisloe Cup
articles.summary: New Zealand retain the Bledisloe Cup for a 23rd straight year as they power past Australia to extend their remarkable unbeaten run at Eden Park.
body: The All Blacks have not lost at the venue since 1994, with a dominant second-half display increasing their unbeaten run in Auckland to 54 Tests.
Australia remained in touch at half-time at 17-14 down but New Zealand blew the visitors away after the break, scoring five tries.

Peter Lakai, Tupou Vaa'i, Cam Roigard, Codie Taylor, Leroy Carter, Josh Moorby and Will Jordan all scored as fly-half Damian McKenzie kicked 15 points to help the All Blacks retain the trophy which is contested annually between the two nations.
Victory halted a three-match losing streak for the All Blacks after the 3-1 series defeat by world champions South Africa this summer.

articles.title: Wallabies blown away by All Blacks blitz as Bledisloe Cup misery extends to 24th year
articles.summary: New Zealand 50-19 Australia to continue unbeaten run at Eden Park. Les Kiss’s side start bright but given reality check in second half. New Zealand preserved rugby’s established hierarchy with a 50-19 blowout victory over Australia that secures the Bledisloe Cup for a 24th year and pushes the All…
body: The Wallabies lost touch with their hosts in the second half despite a valiant but futile defensive performance led by the captain Harry Wilson, who had scored a try just before half-time to keep his side in the contest.

Les Kiss’s side will return home bruised and disappointed, with their unbeaten run extinguished at six matches. Most of all, however, they will rue a missed opportunity early in the second half that marked the match’s decisive point.

An attacking lineout five metres from the All Blacks’ tryline was comfortably brought to ground, but the Wallabies’ forwards were over-eager in forming the maul. The ensuing obstruction penalty and the All Blacks’ patience in possession flipped the field, and beginning with a try for their scrumhalf Cam Roigard, the hosts were soon out of reach.

Wilson said the result was disappointing. “We came in tonight with real belief that we’d get the result and we didn’t,” he told Stan Sport. “We’ve been on a good trajectory, we’ve gotten some good results, six games in a row [unbeaten], and this was probably a setback for us because we didn’t win those big moments and as a team we try to pride ourselves on that.

articles.title: ‘I’m supposed to be here’: Angel Reese’s road from ridicule to the WNBA finals
articles.summary: After years of mockery and doubts about her game, Reese has helped carry Atlanta to the WNBA’s biggest stage. Her critics might want to start forming an apology queue. A lot of folks owe Angel Reese an apology after Friday night. They should probably form an orderly queue.
body: Not that the bad-faith take merchants who have spent three years gleefully circulating her missed layups, likening her occasionally awkward footwork to “Bambi on ice” and marveling at the supposed comic genius of “mebounds” are likely to join it. The right-wing culture warriors who turned one of the WNBA’s most naturally gifted rebounders into a punchline were never particularly interested in an honest assessment of her basketball abilities. But after Friday the punch line has never worn thinner.

Reese’s career has been measured against Caitlin Clark’s almost from the moment the two became household names, their rivalry inflated into a culture-war proxy battle that neither player could fully control. Now Reese has reached the WNBA finals before her more celebrated contemporary, a delicious reversal for those who have spent three seasons insisting she didn’t belong in the same conversation. Not that basketball achievement is require to be a zero-sum proposition.

articles.title: NI debut 'something I thought had passed' - Elmore
articles.summary: Northern Ireland's World Cup hopes may have all but come to an end against Portugal, but for Kess Elmore the 4-0 defeat marks the start of a long-awaited international journey.
body: After a ruthless first-half display from Portugal in Larne gave them a comfortable advantage at the break, Elmore's half-time introduction made an impact for Northern Ireland, who were much improved after the interval.

Elmore was a surprise call-up for the play-off double header against world number 22-ranked Portugal after having been involved in an NI training camp in 2021 and thought her chance to pull on a green shirt was over.
"I wasn't expecting Michael to call me. It was in the back of my mind, but definitely something that I kind of thought had passed," Elmore said.

"I've played in a lot of teams with a lot of different formations, tactics and, over the years, I have gained a real understanding of the game. So, hopefully I can bring a bit of that experience into the squad because we do have a young squad and I bring an attacking presence.

articles.title: Crocker sets sights on route back to the top
articles.summary: Lewis Crocker is looking forward and not back at his world title defeat by Liam Paro as he prepares for his return against Owen Cooper in December at Belfast's 02.
body: The flight home from Australia in June was a little longer for Lewis Crocker as he pondered his defeat by Liam Paro in his first defence of the IBF welterweight champion.
A storming finish by the Belfast man was not enough to turn things around as all three judges gave Paro a 115-113 decision and the Australian realised his dream of becoming a two-weight champion.

Crocker grew into that fight and seemed on the brink of finding a finish in the late rounds, but Paro held on and Crocker lost his grip on the title he won last September in Belfast's Windsor Park against Paddy Donovan - his record slipping to 22 wins with one loss.

"Shoulda, woulda, coulda," is how the 29-year-old reflects on that night in Brisbane - one in which he was so near yet so far away, yet his first career defeat has not dented confidence, but only served to fuel his desire to rise again.

articles.title: Three tied atop bunched up leaderboard entering final round at 2026 Baycurrent Classic
articles.summary: Catch up on everything you missed overnight at the PGA Tour's Baycurrent Classic in Japan, where there's a logjam on the leaderboard after 54 holes.
body: Three players are tied atop the leaderboard and five more are just one shot back after three rounds at the PGA Tour's 2026 Baycurrent Classic in Japan. A trio of Americans ― Michael Brennan, Zach Bauchou and Jacob Bridgeman ― share the lead at 13 under entering the final day at Yokahama Country Club near Tokyo.
Brennan shook off a rough finish to the second round and made the biggest move of the three co-leaders on Saturday, signing for a 6-under 65 tied for the lowest round of the day.

"I played good golf. I've been playing good golf all week," Brennan said. "I played good golf yesterday, I was 6 under through 17 and made a six on the last, which was a bummer. So it was great to save par today. Been hitting my irons really well. Had a couple 7-iron plus irons that I've hit pretty tight and made some birdies from that distance, which is always nice to do. I feel like you're stealing one when you do that. Hit some good putts, rolling it really nicely, so I'm looking forward to tomorrow."

articles.title: 'You will see me back' - Smith vows 2027 return after Swiss Darts Trophy win
articles.summary: Former world champion Michael Smith says he plans on "playing 100 per cent of the tournaments" in 2027 after an opening win at the Swiss Darts Trophy.
body: 'Bully Boy' Smith fought back from 3-1 down to beat Rob Owen, hitting 50 per cent of his doubles in just his fourth European Tour event of the season.
"I've missed this. I want to apologise and also make a promise in 2027 I will be playing 100 per cent of the tournaments. You will see me back," said the 2023 world champion.
Smith is chasing down the final spots in the European Championship race and the St Helens thrower beat Owen 6-4 to set up a meeting with Jermaine Wattimena for a place in Sunday's action.

Rob Cross was Friday's standout performer for the second event in a row, averaging 105.95 in his 6-3 success against Mario Vandenbogaerde and will take on Luke Woodhouse on the back of his brilliant opening round performance at the World Grand Prix.

articles.title: Protect College Sports Act passes Senate, headed to House | Wydeven column
articles.summary: As a kid, I remember being so excited when we first got cable. I loved college hoops, and ESPN aired a ton of Big East games. The network signed its first national television deal with the conference in 1980, just a year after both the network and the sports league were founded.
body: The conference touted some of the best players in the country, including Georgetown’s Patrick Ewing, Syracuse’s Dwayne “The Pearl” Washington, and St. John’s Chris Mullins. It was great to see these rivalries develop as players faced each other multiple times over several seasons.

Unfortunately, those college rivalries have greatly diminished over the years. Major conferences have had huge restructuring over TV deals. It’s weird to think that the Big 10, which is rooted in the Midwest, has multiple teams on both coasts.

Personal rivalries changed forever, too, after COVID. Previously, if a college athlete switched schools, they had to sit out a year before playing for their new team. In 2021, the rules were changed to allow unlimited transfers without having to sit out.

In that same year, the NCAA allowed players to be paid for their name, image and likeness. So, college athletes could finally earn money from endorsements, sponsorships, social media, and personal appearances without losing their athletic eligibility.

articles.summary: Jarrod Bowen saw his 91st-minute penalty saved as West Ham missed the chance to move top of the Sky Bet Championship after a 1-1 draw with QPR.
body: Nicolas Madsen put Rangers 1-0 up, rolling home a penalty awarded in highly controversial circumstances.
But the Hammers came alive as the conclusion approached, with Bowen slamming in his seventh goal of the season to equalise after his first shot was blocked.
In the 90th minute, Amadou Mbengue tugged the shirt of Pablo in the penalty area and Bowen had the chance to win it from the spot.
But Pierce Charles dived low to his left to keep out the initial effort, then reacted in a flash to tip Arne Engels' follow-up over the bar.
